text:
People Ops: Heads up — starting Mon May 4 we’re rolling out a 48-hour auto-approval SLA for routine PTO requests. Managers will have 48 hours to respond; if no response, the request auto-approves. Managers can opt-out per-request or set a default opt-out in manager settings. This rollout also includes new audit logging for cross-border travel approvals. Short doc + FAQ: https://intranet.redwood.ai/policies/pto-sla :sparkles:

Maya (HR Lead): Posting the full policy doc in #docs and the intranet link above. I’ll host a short Q&A Wed 11:00 PT. Added a manager opt-out checklist to the doc.

Diego (EM): Does the auto-approve apply to oncall recovery day requests? Those often come last-minute.

People Ops: Good question — oncall recovery days are marked as a special request type and will NOT auto-approve. The system reads the request category at submission. If you select 'oncall recovery', it stays manual.

Samir (Manager): @People Ops how does opt-out work in practice? Is it per-request, per-manager, or team-level?

People Ops: Opt-out is per-request by default and managers can set a team-level default in their Manager Settings. We’re also adding an org-level override for Legal/Compliance for sensitive roles. The UI update for defaults ships in the next deploy.

Lina (Legal): Please ensure audit logs capture the business justification for cross-border travel, plus country and duration. We need an immutable trail for compliance reviews.

People Ops: Noted — audit logs will include request_id, requestor, approver (or auto-approve flag), timestamp, travel country, duration, and a short justification field. Example log snippet included below.

People Ops (code): ```
req_id=pt-23851 user=diego approver=auto timestamp=2385123472 country=DE duration=3d reason="client on-site"
```

calendar-bot: Reminder: PTO policy town hall Wed 11:00 PT in All-Hands room.

Diego (EM): If multiple people request the same critical day and the system auto-approves, will that create scheduling conflicts?

People Ops: The system surfaces a conflict warning at submission if the team's OOO threshold is exceeded. Auto-approval will still proceed unless a manager has set opt-out for the request or the conflict threshold triggers an automatic hold. We’ll also send a conflict alert DM to managers and the requestor.

Samir (Manager): :thumbsup: Will managers get a digest of auto-approved requests or only real-time alerts?

People Ops: By default managers get a daily digest plus real-time alerts for conflicts and high-risk travel. Admins can switch to a weekly summary or turn off digests in Manager Settings.

Maya (HR Lead): I’ll run a manager training session Thu 2:00 PT to walk through the opt-out flows and inbox/digest settings. Invite going out shortly.

People Ops: Rollout timeline: beta (opt-in) next week; org-wide enforcement in 6 weeks. If you manage a team with cross-border travel or compliance constraints, please DM us to opt into the pilot early. Questions? Ping @People Ops or reply in thread.
